text:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: p99 latency breach detected for /v1/streaming/generate - SLO p99 > 3.0s (current ~6.1s) — error budget at risk. Automations: opened incident IRC-1964000000, paging on-call. https://grafana.internal/streams?panelId=12

pagerduty-bot: Paging devon-oncall (primary). Incident severity: sev2. Pager: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-1964000000

devon-oncall: I got the page, starting triage. Observed spike at 01:45 UTC, p95 ~1.2s p99 ~6s, tail shows streaming stalls (clients reporting stalls around token 512). Anyone on infra?

sophie-sre: on it. Looking at node allocation and recent evictions. Early hypothesis: a handful of GPU nodes showing elevated ECC counts and thermal throttle events. Correlating logs now.

aj-ml: Noticed an error surge in model runtime logs: a repeated KV-cache miss + long GC pause (~200ms) on worker shards. Might amplify tail latency for streaming.

maria-ops: Pulling container and host metrics. Two nodes in cluster-gpu-us-west2 show sustained power draw spikes and fan speeds pegged. Node IDs: gpu-az2-n12, gpu-az2-n13.

infra-bot: Attached relevant graphs: CPU, GPU temp, ECC events. Short link: https://grafana.internal/d/abc123/streaming-tail?orgId=1

devon-oncall: OK, plan: (1) divert new streaming traffic away from az2-n12/13 via routing rule for 10m, (2) scale up warm fallback pool (cpu-only model-compat) by +3 replicas, (3) drain the two suspect nodes for inspection, (4) keep user-visible degrade mode if needed. Who can run the drain?

tim-dev: I can run the drain. Command to cordon + drain: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-az2-n12 -n inference
kubectl drain gpu-az2-n12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data -n inference
kubectl cordon gpu-az2-n13 -n inference
kubectl drain gpu-az2-n13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data -n inference
```
I'll start now and watch for eviction backpressure.

maria-ops: Noted. While draining, I'll flip routing using route pool 'streaming-high' to exclude those nodes. Patch route: 
```
PATCH /api/v1/routing/pools/streaming-high
payload: { "exclude_nodes": ["gpu-az2-n12","gpu-az2-n13"], "duration_s": 600 }
```
Applying in 20s.

sophie-sre: Correlation from dmesg on gpu-az2-n12: repeated ECC corrected error bursts then thermal scaling: 
```
[ 12345.678] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 12346.001] kernel: GPU temp rising 92C -> throttle
[ 12346.345] edac: ECC error: corrected 24 bits
```
This matches hardware flake + thermal. If ECC bursts persist, we should remove node from rotation until replacement.

aj-ml: Also seeing a spike in our runtime's async retry loop which stacks up tokens when GPU stalls. This produces a backlog that increases p99 for streaming sessions. Temporary mitigations: reduce concurrency per worker and increase per-request timeout fallback to CPU path for streaming once token latency > 2s.

devon-oncall: Good. Implement two immediate mitigations: lower worker concurrency for streaming pods by 30% and scale CPU fallback pool +3. Who can change concurrency?

maria-ops: I can update the deployment autoscaler profile now. Patch snippet: 
```
PATCH /api/v1/deployments/streaming-worker
payload: { "concurrency": 70 }  # from 100
```
Applying.

infra-bot: Automation note: started auto-fallback on 12% of requests hitting >2.5s threshold — switching them to model-compat cpu path.

sophie-sre: Drains completed on n12, n13. Observing fewer ECC events after node is isolated (makes sense). Rebooting both nodes for hardware vendor diagnostics.

aj-ml: After routing change + scale + concurrency reduction, p95 back to ~0.9s, p99 down to ~2.4s. Still above SLO but trending. Streaming stalls reduced per logs.

devon-oncall: Great. Next: open hardware ticket and schedule replacement for n12 (ECC corrected counts exceeded threshold). Create incident ticket with hardware team and tag for expedited swap. I'll update PD incident notes.

infra-bot: Hardware ticket created: HT-48712, priority P1. Vendor diagnostics requested.

cs-liaison: Heads-up: CS reporting a customer (enterprise-acct-42) noticed interrupted streams and submitted a ticket. Impact window: 01:44-01:56 UTC ~12m, approx 0.8% of their requests affected. I'll coordinate postmortem communications.

devon-oncall: Logging customer impact in incident doc. Action items: (A) Continue monitoring p99 for another 30m, (B) keep fallback pool at +3 until nodes replaced, (C) validate model output parity for fallback path (aj), (D) run postmortem and update customers with timeline.

aj-ml: I'll run a small eval on the cpu fallback outputs against the streaming model to check regressions. Quick diff job: 
```
./eval/run_compare --model gpu/streaming-v2 --fallback cpu/streaming-compat --samples 200
```
Posting results in 10m.

maria-ops: Rolling reboot logs show pgpu driver recovered but ECC counts on n12 still above threshold on persistent query. Will keep node offline.

sophie-sre: I'm adding a short-term alert refinement: if ECC corrected errors > 10 in 5m then auto-isolate node. That would've caught this earlier. Pushing rule now.

devon-oncall: Good idea. Also let's add a chart to the runbook about combined signal: ECC errs + thermal spike + increased retry loop backlog -> triage step A.

infra-bot: Note added to incident timeline: mitigation applied, fallback scale and routing patch at 01:47 UTC.

aj-ml: Eval results: fallback outputs have minor formatting differences but no functional regressions for 200 samples. Confidence=high.

devon-oncall: OK. Customer comms draft: "We experienced a partial streaming degradation due to GPU node hardware errors leading to elevated tail latency. We diverted traffic and enabled CPU fallback, which restored normal levels within ~6 minutes. We're replacing the affected hardware and will follow up with a postmortem." CS, please review.

cs-liaison: Reviewed, adding ETA for replacement and offer of credits where appropriate.

maria-ops: Monitoring now shows p99 stabilizing ~1.1s, p95 ~0.85s. I'll keep routing exclusion in place until vendor confirms swap.

sophie-sre: After-action: propose two follow-ups: (1) auto-isolate on ECC+thermals (as pushed), (2) backpressure knob in runtime to shed streaming to fallback earlier to avoid backlog growth. I'll own (2).

devon-oncall: Solid. I'll wrap incident and schedule postmortem for tomorrow 15:00 UTC. Thanks all. Marking incident as mitigated — keeping incident open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
